items.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: Bob Brookmeyer... was writing a four movement suite for Clark Terry’s seventieth birthday... I’m behind... I’ve got the seventieth birthday this week, a four movement suite for Clark Terry

ctx.x: Oh. They would send you the —

Yeah. And Brookmeyer, that’s how I actually got to know Bob was he was writing a four movement suite for Clark Terry’s seventieth birthday. And I called Bob because his recording called “Electricity” had come out and it wasn’t available in the states. And Fred Sturm had said, “Oh here’s Bob’s number, just call him he’ll send you one. He’s a nice guy.” And I didn’t know, I thought because Mulligan and Brookmeyer — Gerry Mulligan and Brookmeyer were close, so I thought well Mulligan is known to be difficult and…

it was incredible because I mean the hand copied parts was a stack of music like this. And I hired two guys. And one or the other was always here, ‘round the clock, as I was copying, in the dining room, proofreading every page. Because the deadline was so close. Every time I finished a page I’d give it to them and they’d check it, and then finally —
